transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you—what has been bothering you lately that made you decide to come in today?

Lately I’ve been making a lot of careless mistakes at work, even on things I know how to do, and it’s starting to cause problems. I’ll miss small details in emails or reports, then have to redo things, and it’s gotten frustrating enough that I thought I should get it checked out.

Along with the mistakes at work, do you more often notice your mind constantly worrying and feeling tense, or do you mainly feel down, low in motivation, or is it more that your attention easily drifts and you can’t stay focused even when you’re interested?

It’s mostly that my attention drifts and I can’t stay focused, even on things I actually care about. I’ll be in the middle of reading something or listening to someone and realize my mind has gone somewhere else, and then I miss parts and have to backtrack.

Have you had this kind of trouble paying attention and making careless mistakes since you were a child or teenager, or is it something that only started more recently in adult life, for example in the past few months or years?

I feel like it’s been there as long as I can remember, even back in elementary school. Teachers used to write comments about “careless mistakes” or not checking my work, and I remember losing points on tests for things I actually knew but rushed or overlooked.

Outside of work and school tasks, do you also find it hard to stay organized or follow through on everyday things like chores, errands, or managing your schedule, and has this caused problems in your relationships or daily life over the years?

Yeah, that’s definitely an issue for me. I’ll forget to do chores I said I’d handle, miss appointments or pay bills late unless someone reminds me, and it’s caused some tension with my partner and family because it comes across like I’m being irresponsible or not listening.

Have your attention and follow-through problems clearly worsened after any specific stressful or traumatic event in your life, or have they stayed about the same level of difficulty across different situations and life periods?

They’ve pretty much been the same kind of problem throughout my life, just showing up in different ways at school, at home, and now at work. There wasn’t a specific stressful or traumatic event that suddenly made it worse—it’s more like it’s always been there in the background.

opening_question.question: Hello, it’s good to meet you—what has been bothering you lately that made you decide to come in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a lifelong pattern, beginning in elementary school, of inattention, careless mistakes, difficulty sustaining focus, and poor follow-through that occurs across multiple settings (school, home, work) and causes clear functional impairment in occupational and interpersonal domains. There is no indication of a mood or anxiety disorder driving the symptoms, and the presentation is consistent with Attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder, predominantly inattentive type.
